content:
Peacock has renewed The Traitors for three seasons, in addition to the upcoming season returning in 2027. Alan Cumming is set to return as host. The series is a nail-biting psychological adventure in which treachery and deceit are the name of the game. A distinguished roster of famous faces, notable figures, top competitors, and reality icons play the ultimate murder mystery game. Hosted by award-winning Alan Cumming at an ancient castle set deep in the Scottish Highlands, players work together on a series of exhilarating missions to build a substantial prize fund. Hidden amongst the Faithfuls are the Traitors, whose goal is to eliminate the Faithful and claim the prize for themselves. Under the cover of darkness, the Traitors murder the Faithful one by one in a treacherous spree, while the Faithful try to uncover the Traitors and banish them from the game. If the Faithful banish all the Traitors, they will share the prize fund, but if a Traitor (or Traitors) makes it to the end, they will steal all the money. Before the next season of Peacock’s The Traitors, NBC will debut The Traitors: New Blood on September 17. 

Heated Rivalry has added even more cast for its upcoming second season. Joining the HBO Max series are Brendan Morgan, David Tomlinson, Gerry Dee, Michelle Mylett, Lauren Chan, and Nick Stahl. 

Saturday Night Live has added two featured players to the cast. Joining the 52nd season are Saidah Belo-Osagie and Grace Reiter. The new season premieres September 26 on NBC with host Jalen Brunson and musical guest KATSEYE. 

Scrubs returns for a second season September 30 on ABC. J.D., Turk and Elliot have leveled up from interns to icons at Sacred Heart. Now, the respected doctors inspire the next generation while balancing the ups and downs of working in a hospital. Together with characters new and old, they are navigating this next chapter with laughter, heart and some surprises along the way. 

Jefferson White joins the upcoming second season of Marshals in a recurring role. White will reprise his Yellowstone role as fan-favorite Jimmy Hurdstrom, a good-hearted yet rough-around-the-edges ranch hand who evolved from a troubled criminal into a resilient, proud cowboy. 

Season two of Haunted Hotel premieres October 9 on Netflix. New ghosts. New employees. New undefined evils that we haven’t even discovered yet! A single mother tries to run the world’s most haunted hotel with her ghost brother, two kids, a demon trapped in a little boy’s body, and an ever growing collection of ghosts, monsters, and supernatural disasters. 

HBO Max has ordered drama series How to Survive Without Me. The drama stars series regulars Ray Romano, Kaley Cuoco, Joshua Jackson, Julia Schlaepfer, Jack Ball, Kylar Miranda, Julian Grey, Scarlett Abinante, Tommy Dewey, Matthew Kellison, Colette Porch, Ella Rubin, and Rita Wilson as members of the De Angelis family. Romano plays the family’s patriarch and Wilson plays the deceased matriarch. In the wake of matriarch Beverly’s passing, the De Angelis family have begun to drift, unsure how to manage their complicated, evolving lives without her guidance, but in true Beverly fashion, she found a way to keep running the show from the beyond. Should they wish to experience Beverly’s final work, the family must find the time – and make the effort – to remain connected and be there for each other through all of life’s challenges yet to come. 

Madonna will open the 2026 Video Music Awards (VMAs) for her first live performance at the show in 23 years. Hosted by Snoop Dogg, the VMAs will air live from Los Angeles on Sunday, Sept. 27 (7:30-9:30 PM, ET/4:30-6:30 PM, PT) on CBS. 

Breaking the Deadlock returns with a new episode “AI: Who’s in Control?” October 27 on PBS. In this new episode, eight panelists face a series of challenging dilemmas: in a town fractured over data centers, will a couple take a huge cash offer from a company primed to build one? Is it acceptable for a town to use AI surveillance cameras to identify people who might commit a crime, but haven’t yet? 

The Amazing Race: 25 Years Around the World premieres September 29 on CBS. The one-hour special celebrates 25 years of The Amazing Race with memorable moments from the Entertainment Tonight Vault, never-before-seen footage and new interviews. It offers a behind-the-scenes look at the challenges, destinations and contestants that have defined the series. Host Phil Keoghan sits down to reflect on the show’s history and share stories from its journey around the globe. Other featured guests include co-creator and executive producer Elise Doganieri and fan-favorite contestants, such as season seven winners Uchenna Agu and Joyce Robinson, who memorably shaved her head during the competition; season 32 winners Will Jardell and James Wallington; Claire Champlin and Brook Roberts, who unforgettably got hit in the head with a flying watermelon; the cowboys, Jet and Cord McCoy; Flight Time and Big Easy; among others. Season 39 of The Amazing Race will feature a two night premiere September 30 and October 1 on CBS. 

The Country Music Association (CMA) announced today that it is producing CMA Presents I Will Always Love You: A Celebration of Dolly Parton, a two-hour television event in tribute to Dolly Parton, airing live Wednesday, Oct. 21 (9:00-11:00 p.m. EDT) on ABC and Disney+. Following her passing on Aug. 25, the special will be a joyful, emotional celebration of the artist, songwriter, entertainer, humanitarian and entrepreneur whose music and generosity carried her from the mountains of east Tennessee into the hearts of generations around the world, told through performances, archival footage and personal stories that trace her extraordinary journey to becoming one of the most beloved entertainers and philanthropists in American history. 

The Great British Baking Show Collection 14 premieres September 25 on Netflix. On your Marks, Get set… Bake! The Great British Baking Show is back with a brand new season – a brand new judge, and a brand new batch of talented amateur bakers from across the UK. In the iconic white tent, they’ll take on the ultimate baking challenges – from showstopping celebration cakes to perfect pastries – all under the watchful eyes of judges Paul Hollywood and Nigella Lawson. Each week, the bakers face Signature, Technical, and Showstopper challenges designed to test their creativity, skill, and nerves. One baker will be sent home, and one will rise to become this season’s winner.

Comedy special Kate Berlant: Parmesan premieres October 16 on HBO. Seamlessly weaving through personal stories and stream-of-consciousness epiphanies, Kate offers up razor-sharp reflections on everything from the moon, to her destructive relationship to technology, to the evolving nature of sexuality. Filmed at the historic Plaza Nightclub in Los Angeles, it is a hilarious tour-de-force that skewers the many contradictions of modern life and the art of stand-up comedy itself. 

Season three of Helluva Boss premieres October 14, followed by two episodes weekly through October 28. The new season follows Blitzo and the I.M.P. crew as they continue taking jobs across Earth and Hell, while navigating their increasingly complex personal lives. While Blitzo and Stolas struggle to find out where they stand, Millie and Moxxie prepare for a life-changing surprise, and Loona takes on a larger role at I.M.P. Along the way, the team is thrown into a string of increasingly chaotic adventures that test both their skills as assassins and their relationships with one another. As old enemies resurface and new opportunities arise, Season Three delivers Helluva Boss’s signature blend of explosive comedy, over-the-top violence, and heartfelt character drama, as the team discovers that some of their biggest challenges can’t be solved with a weapon (unfortunately). 

Season two of Sacrifice premieres September 30 on Paramount+. The second season of Sacrifice follows Hernandez as she navigates the world of high finance while attempting to save her family birthright. As Beverly Rucker’s (Erica Ash) run for Mayor in a recall election forces her moral center, Dom Mayfield (Juan Antonio) finds the road to legitimacy and respectability a much more difficult path. 

Three part docuseries The Serial Killer Connection premieres October 7 on ID. Decades after marrying Richard “Marc” Evonitz at a young age, Bonnie Lou learns that her former husband had been living a horrifying double life as a serial killer – with his deadly secret ultimately revealed after Kara Robinson Chamberlain’s courageous escape from captivity. Years later, an unexpected connection sparked by a social media trend brings the two women together, transforming shared trauma into a determined quest for answers. United by a singular mission, the ex-wife and survivor of a serial killer unite in their determination to uncover the untold life and crimes of Evontiz and as they dig deeper, they confront the chilling possibility that the full scope of his crimes has yet to be revealed. 

Love Is Blind: Netherlands premieres September 30 on Netflix. Hosted by Nicolette van Dam and Bas Smit, 30 single men and women enter the pods in the hope of finding a genuine, lasting connection, without ever seeing the person they’re talking to. They date in individual pods, separated by a thin wall, and have the chance to build an emotional connection before meeting face-to-face. If they feel they’ve found the right person, they can even get engaged before seeing each other for the first time. From there, the couples meet in person and find out whether their connection can survive outside the pods. They travel together, move in together, plan their weddings, and navigate the challenges of building a relationship in the real world. And then comes the ultimate test: the altar. Will they say ‘I do’ and prove that love really is blind, or will they decide to go their separate ways?
